title: How Desert Foxes Keep Cool
passage:
The fennec fox is the smallest fox in the world, yet its ears can grow longer than fifteen centimetres. Those enormous ears are not only for hearing insects moving beneath the sand; they also release body heat, which helps the fox survive daytime temperatures that would exhaust most mammals.

Fennec foxes rest in burrows during the hottest hours and hunt after sunset, when the desert cools. Thick fur on the soles of their feet protects them from burning sand, while their pale coat reflects sunlight instead of absorbing it.

Scientists believe these adaptations developed slowly over many generations. Although the fennec fox rarely drinks, it obtains most of the water it needs from the plants and insects it eats.
